items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: I had a friend called Philip Sherman who lived across the river from me

ctx.x: Yeah - Defiance, Ohio and, uh, we would harmonize and this is when we were kids of about seven years old - eight years old and it was amazing to find that you could find the harmony - like "Auld Lang Syne" and barber shop chords and barber shop harmony to songs that we used to play or sing and that's when I got the idea that it was easy for me to find what would be, in a growing up quartet, would be the baritone part. And, we had a kid that could also sing wonderful tenor and it was amazing what we put together…

play the mandolin and he used to play mandolin and sing little songs along with it and that fascinated me. So, it took quite a bit of doing on my part because he didn't want to be bothered with any kids, I'm sure at that time. But, I'd ask him if he could just please show me how to make a scale. So, he actually taught me how to run the scale on this thing and, from there, I got to play all the old time songs. I could pick them out by myself after I learned to do the scale - the half-tone scale and regular scale…

on Saturday nights, I'd play this hoedown music and then they started throwing in what they call "round music", that was fox trot and I got to learn the chords and play some of those songs. And, of course, they didn't have much choice about me because I was the only banjo player in town - so, they either had to have me or no banjo. So, I was pretty awful at first.
